role: Business Intelligence Engineer II, Fulfillment Optimization
responsibilities: Design and own explainability frameworks that decompose model outputs across multiple Fulfillment Optimization systems into interpretable, actionable signals for science, engineering, and business stakeholders
Build analytical pipelines and dashboards that monitor output shape and quality, detect anomalies, and quantify the relationship between model behavior and fulfillment performance
Partner with BIE and analytics teams to align on shared metrics, enable self-service data access, and connect optimization insights with network-level reporting
Trace data lineage from source systems through model transformation to downstream consumption, and translate findings into recommendations that inform team prioritization decisions

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: deliver efficient, testable, and maintainable solutions that balance speed of delivery with long-term reliability
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Testable, reliable solutions, lineage tracing and anomaly monitoring outweigh the single speed reference.
evidence.domain_risk: quantify how output shape and quality connect to fulfillment performance, transportation cost, and customer delivery promise
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Operational fulfilment analytics affects cost and delivery decisions without regulatory or financial-reporting framing, so it is moderate.
evidence.collaboration_width: BIE and analytics teams; research scientists; engineering
evidence.data_team_maturity: Partner with BIE and analytics teams to align on shared metrics, enable self-service data access, and connect optimization insights with network-level reporting
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Multiple BIE and analytics teams aligning on shared measurement inside a large science organisation is mature.
evidence.jd_authorship: Design and own explainability frameworks that decompose model outputs across multiple Fulfillment Optimization systems into interpretable, actionable signals for science, engineering, and business stakeholders
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The bullets and summary describe a specific problem (explaining optimisation model outputs) in concrete terms.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: into interpretable, actionable signals for science, engineering, and business stakeholders
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Science, engineering and business stakeholders are served with roughly equal weight.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role owns its analytical layer and translates findings into "recommendations that inform team prioritization decisions".
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The role explains optimisation model outputs but is not asked to use AI tools or build data for AI systems.
evidence.testing_framing: Build analytical pipelines and dashboards that monitor output shape and quality, detect anomalies
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Quality monitoring and anomaly detection are responsibilities the candidate owns.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: ensuring stakeholders understand not just what the numbers say but where they come from
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Understanding and reliability matter, framed around insight rather than risk control.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: You are building the analytical foundation that tells us whether our models are producing the outcomes we expect
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: A new explainability layer is built on top of existing optimisation systems.
evidence.loss_aversion: ensuring stakeholders understand not just what the numbers say but where they come from — understanding, not risk, is the framing.
